/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1705.title: fix(config): keep output.log, hk.log and patches in the repository's git dir
/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/1705.body:
Fixes #1703.

hk kept `output.log`, `hk.log` and stash backup `patches/` in one per-user directory (`~/.local/state/hk`), so every repository and worktree shared them. A failure in repo A could print `See ~/.local/state/hk/output.log` while the file held another repo's output, and patch rotation could delete another repo's backups.

## Behavior

Inside a repository, state now defaults to the git directory:

| State | Default | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `patches/` | `<common-git-dir>/hk/patches` | repository, shared by linked worktrees |
| `output.log` | `<git-dir>/hk/output.log` | one checkout |
| `hk.log` | `<git-dir>/hk/hk.log` | one checkout |

- Explicit `HK_STATE_DIR`, `HK_OUTPUT_FILE` and `HK_LOG_FILE` still win; with `HK_STATE_DIR` set everything lives there as before. Outside a repository the platform state dir remains the fallback.
- Git never tracks files under its git dir, so no `.gitignore` change is needed. The `hk` directories are still created `0700`.
- In a shared `HK_STATE_DIR`, patch files are named after the repository root (not the current subdirectory) and rotation only matches `<name>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-...`, so `app` no longer claims `app-web`'s patches.

## Validation

New bats tests cover per-checkout `output.log` across a linked worktree, patches shared via the common git dir, and rotation not touching a sibling repo's patches in a shared `HK_STATE_DIR`.

nodes.title: fix(config): keep output.log, hk.log and patches in the repository's git dir
nodes.body:
Fixes #1703.

hk kept `output.log`, `hk.log` and stash backup `patches/` in one per-user directory (`~/.local/state/hk`), so every repository and worktree shared them. A failure in repo A could print `See ~/.local/state/hk/output.log` while the file held another repo's output, and patch rotation could delete another repo's backups.

## Behavior

Inside a repository, state now defaults to the git directory:

| State | Default | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `patches/` | `<common-git-dir>/hk/patches` | repository, shared by linked worktrees |
| `output.log` | `<git-dir>/hk/output.log` | one checkout |
| `hk.log` | `<git-dir>/hk/hk.log` | one checkout |

- Explicit `HK_STATE_DIR`, `HK_OUTPUT_FILE` and `HK_LOG_FILE` still win; with `HK_STATE_DIR` set everything lives there as before. Outside a repository the platform state dir remains the fallback.
- Git never tracks files under its git dir, so no `.gitignore` change is needed. The `hk` directories are still created `0700`.
- In a shared `HK_STATE_DIR`, patch files are named after the repository root (not the current subdirectory) and rotation only matches `<name>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-...`, so `app` no longer claims `app-web`'s patches.

## Validation

New bats tests cover per-checkout `output.log` across a linked worktree, patches shared via the common git dir, and rotation not touching a sibling repo's patches in a shared `HK_STATE_DIR`.

commit.messageHeadline: fix(config): keep state in the repository's git dir instead of a global dir

nodes.body:
[P1] **State uses the wrong repository**

`REPO_DIRS` ignores `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`, unlike `Git::new()`. In supported YADM-style setups without a `.git` directory, logs and backups still fall back to the shared platform directory, leaving this fix incomplete. If the current directory belongs to another repository, hk instead writes and rotates backups in that repository's git directory. Resolve the same repository as `Git::new()`, including Git environment variables.

[P1] **Other accounts cannot save backups**

Moving state into the shared git directory makes the private `0700` directory belong to the first account that runs hk. In a repository with `core.sharedRepository=group`, another group member cannot enter that directory, so hk cannot save their logs, failed-command output, or patch backups. Previously each account had its own writable state directory. Keep private state writable for each account, for example with separate account-owned directories.

### State discovery ignores GIT_DIR

**Medium Severity**

`REPO_DIRS` finds the repository with `git2::Repository::discover` from the current directory and never reads `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE`. `Git::new` and `find_git_path` already honor those variables, so checkout logs and stash patches can be written under a different repository than the one hk is operating on.

<sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a7e539f88c349edd89d346aa9b54dcc6fb40d7c6. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

### Shared repos cannot write state

**Medium Severity**

`create_state_dir_all` still creates `.git/hk` and `.git/hk/patches` as `0700`. Those paths now live in a git directory that `core.sharedRepository` shares across accounts, so the first user to create them blocks every other account from writing `output.log`, `hk.log`, or stash backups.

<sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a7e539f88c349edd89d346aa9b54dcc6fb40d7c6. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor**

`REPO_DIRS` converts any error from opening the repository into `None`, so hk falls back to the platform state directory instead of reporting the failure. Is that fallback intentional? If so, no change is needed here.
